> round, use FOR and play Skin of Steel.

Bringing in another superior discipline is not a solution...
especially when it dramatically cuts down the options for your crypt
to a handful of fatties. Far better is to use what we already know we
have.

So if you want to avoid IG with AUS CEL guns, may I suggest replacing
Eyes of Blades with Sniper Rifles (if you're blocking with AUS) and/or
more maneuvers (I hear CEL has many interesting flavours for those).

Eyes of Blades is probably better used when you're not using guns and
are playing combat avoidance. Instead of your star AUS CEL vampire
packing maneuvers for IG defense, use a few EoB and you don't have to
worry about being out maneuvered (Slammed) or any Murder of Crows that
show up. You do have to worry about the fact that it has a DNR until
untap... so it's not something you really want to rely on. It's that
more than anything that will keep it out of my decks.

> > obvious use is AUS CEL ANI but this discipline combination is scarce :S

Yeah, trying to combo it with environmental damage is another
approach. Still, that DNR is going to get you.

Brent Ross

Messages.Author: bwross
Messages.Body:
On Oct 18, 10:44 pm, The Lasombra <TheLasom...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> It is the same as Bloodform, without the press to end.

Bloodform (at superior) also protects against non-agg environmental
damage like Carrion Crows and Weather Control, but does not extend
protection to any agg damage (strike or retainer).

Eye of Blades (at superior) doesn't stop non-retainer environmental
damage, but does appear to stop both damage and non-damage side-
effects from strikes (but not from retainers, where it only stops
damage). It also stops agg damage (for the damage sources where it'd
work on non-agg as well).

Brent Ross
